findings.title: robots.txt reveals sensitive paths
findings.fix: remove secret paths from robots.txt, block them at the server instead
findings.impact: disallowed admin/backup paths are published to everyone

findings.title: Directory listing enabled
findings.fix: autoindex off; (nginx) / Options -Indexes (Apache)
findings.impact: attackers enumerate backups, uploads and forgotten files

findings.title: security.txt missing
findings.fix: publish /.well-known/security.txt with Contact: mailto:you@domain and Policy: link
findings.impact: researchers have no documented channel to report issues to you

findings.title: Site served over plain HTTP
findings.fix: redirect all HTTP to HTTPS and serve only TLS 1.2+, e.g. nginx: return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
findings.impact: an attacker on the same network reads and edits every request

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy missing
findings.fix: start report-only: Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'self'; report-uri /csp-report, then enforce
findings.impact: injected scripts run freely, XSS impact jumps from leak to takeover

findings.title: Page can be framed (clickjacking)
findings.fix: add_header X-Frame-Options "DENY" always; and CSP frame-ancestors 'none'
findings.impact: an invisible overlay on a trusted page hijacks clicks and inputs

findings.title: Referrer-Policy missing
findings.fix: add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
findings.impact: full URLs (with tokens in query strings) leak to third parties

findings.title: Permissions-Policy missing
findings.fix: add_header Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()" always;
findings.impact: scripts can reach camera, microphone, geolocation without consent gating

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy missing
findings.fix: add_header Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin" always;
findings.impact: cross-origin documents can share a browsing context (Spectre-class risk)

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy missing
findings.fix: add_header Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy "same-site" always; (test PDFs first)
findings.impact: responses can be read cross-origin in no-cors contexts

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options missing
findings.fix: add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
findings.impact: browsers MIME-sniff responses into executable content

findings.title: Sensitive page is cacheable
findings.evidence: no Cache-Control on a sensitive page
findings.fix: add_header Cache-Control "no-store, private" always; on login/account/API responses
findings.impact: shared caches and browsers persist authenticated pages

findings.title: Framework fingerprint header present
findings.fix: suppress it: nginx proxy_hide_header X-Powered-By;, or framework config expose_php=Off / X-Powered-By off
findings.impact: attackers match your exact framework/version to known exploits

findings.title: Server version disclosed in banner
findings.fix: nginx: server_tokens off;, or proxy_hide_header Server; then set a generic Server value at the edge
findings.impact: version-matched exploits (CVE lookups) become one-shot

findings.title: Untrusted Host/X-Forwarded-Host reaches output
findings.fix: build URLs from a configured canonical origin, never from request headers; reject unknown Host values at the proxy
findings.impact: password-reset and absolute links can be poisoned to attacker infrastructure

findings.title: CORS reflects arbitrary Origin
findings.fix: allowlist exact origins server-side, never echo the request Origin; keep Access-Control-Allow-Credentials off unless required
findings.impact: any website can read this origin's responses with the victim's cookies
findings.detail: two different attacker origins were both echoed back

findings.title: Session cookie without HttpOnly
findings.fix: add HttpOnly to all session cookies
findings.impact: any XSS payload reads document.cookie and exfiltrates the session

findings.title: Session cookie without SameSite
findings.fix: add SameSite=Lax (or Strict for state-changing flows)
findings.impact: cross-site requests carry the session, widening CSRF

findings.title: Session cookie issued over HTTP
findings.evidence: session cookie sessionid issued over plain HTTP
findings.fix: serve the site over HTTPS only and set Secure on every session cookie
findings.impact: session identifiers are readable and replayable on the wire

findings.title: Session cookie without HttpOnly
findings.fix: add HttpOnly to all session cookies
findings.impact: any XSS payload reads document.cookie and exfiltrates the session

findings.title: Session cookie without SameSite
findings.fix: add SameSite=Lax (or Strict for state-changing flows)
findings.impact: cross-site requests carry the session, widening CSRF

findings.title: Session cookie issued over HTTP
findings.evidence: session cookie auth issued over plain HTTP
findings.fix: serve the site over HTTPS only and set Secure on every session cookie
findings.impact: session identifiers are readable and replayable on the wire

findings.title: JWT signed with a guessable secret
findings.evidence: signature validates with candidate secret 'secret' (offline check)
findings.fix: switch to RS256/ES256 or a 256-bit random secret, store it in a secret manager, rotate it
findings.impact: attackers forge tokens offline, no login needed
findings.detail: verified offline, no requests to the target

findings.title: JWT has no expiration claim
findings.fix: set short exp (minutes to hours), validate exp/nbf/iss/aud, back long sessions with refresh tokens
findings.impact: tokens live forever, logout and password change do not revoke them

findings.title: Secret or live API key shipped to the browser
findings.evidence: AWS access key ID in served content: AKIAIO**********MPLE (value redacted)
findings.fix: pull the key out of the client bundle at once, rotate it, issue a scoped server-side replacement, restrict the old key
findings.impact: any visitor can read the key and spend your money or your data
findings.detail: client-visible secret: treat as compromised, rotate it and move it server-side

findings.title: Secret or live API key shipped to the browser
findings.evidence: Stripe live secret in served content: sk_liv**********************beef (value redacted)
findings.fix: pull the key out of the client bundle at once, rotate it, issue a scoped server-side replacement, restrict the old key
findings.impact: any visitor can read the key and spend your money or your data
findings.detail: client-visible secret: treat as compromised, rotate it and move it server-side

findings.title: Git repository exposed on the server
findings.fix: remove .git from deployment artifacts, deny dotfiles at the server: location ~ /\.git { deny all; }
findings.impact: the full source tree and history ship to the attacker, secrets inside get harvested

findings.title: Environment file exposed
findings.fix: move .env outside the web root, deny dotfiles, then rotate EVERY secret it ever contained
findings.impact: API keys, DB passwords and tokens are handed over in one request

findings.title: Cloud credentials file exposed
findings.fix: remove the file, rotate those credentials immediately, use an instance role instead of keys on disk
findings.impact: your cloud account is directly compromiseable

findings.title: Configuration file exposed
findings.fix: block config filenames at the server and stop shipping them in builds
findings.impact: internal paths, credentials or feature flags become known

findings.title: Dependency manifest exposed
findings.fix: deny package manifests at the edge; run npm audit / osv-scanner to check those versions yourself first
findings.impact: exact component versions are known, CVE matching becomes one-shot

findings.title: Debug/monitoring endpoint exposed
findings.fix: disable actuator/phpinfo/server-status style endpoints in production, bind them to localhost or auth
findings.impact: runtime config, env values and internal state are disclosed

findings.title: Backup or archive file exposed
findings.fix: delete backups from the web root, store them outside docroot, deny *.bak *.old *.zip *.sql *.tar.gz
findings.impact: source code, databases or keys leak through leftover deploy files

findings.title: Private key file exposed on the server
findings.fix: remove the key from the web root immediately and rotate it (reissue the certificate / API key), store keys outside docroot
findings.impact: attackers decrypt recorded traffic or impersonate your services

findings.title: API documentation exposed publicly
findings.fix: serve OpenAPI/Swagger only in staging or behind auth; block schema paths at the edge
findings.impact: the full API surface, including forgotten endpoints, is handed to attackers

findings.title: Admin interface reachable from the internet
findings.fix: bind admin panels to localhost or a VPN, add IP allowlisting plus MFA, remove them from public DNS
findings.impact: database or server admin panels are brute-force and 0-day targets

findings.title: Stack trace or debug page exposed
findings.evidence:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/server.py", line 42, in handler
KeyError: 'missing'
findings.fix: return generic errors with a correlation ID, keep traces in protected logs, disable debug mode in production
findings.impact: internal paths, framework versions and query shapes leak, aiding follow-up attacks

findings.title: GraphQL introspection enabled in production
findings.fix: disable introspection in production (Apollo: introspection: false; Hasura/GraphQL Yoga: disable for anon roles)
findings.impact: the full schema, including hidden mutations, is enumerable by anyone

findings.title: Reflected cross-site scripting
findings.evidence: raw echo of '<">\'QX5a4fabf36ada0fee' in response body
findings.fix: context-aware output encoding (framework auto-escape), avoid innerHTML, add CSP as a second layer
findings.impact: attacker links hijack any victim's session on your domain

findings.title: Path traversal
findings.fix: canonicalize and verify the resolved path stays under the allowed base dir, allowlist filenames
findings.impact: arbitrary file read: configs, keys, source

findings.title: Possible SQL injection (boolean differential)
findings.evidence: AND 1=1 matches baseline (1.00) while AND 1=2 diverges (0.69)
findings.fix: same fix as error-based SQLi: parameterized queries everywhere
findings.impact: attacker can walk the database one boolean at a time
findings.detail: boolean differential is a strong signal; confirm manually before calling it SQLi

findings.title: Open redirect
findings.fix: allowlist redirect targets (path-only or known hosts), reject scheme-relative and absolute URLs
findings.impact: phishing links borrow your trusted domain

findings.title: Reflected cross-site scripting
findings.evidence: raw echo of '<">\'QX5a4fabf36a8bbcdd' in response body
findings.fix: context-aware output encoding (framework auto-escape), avoid innerHTML, add CSP as a second layer
findings.impact: attacker links hijack any victim's session on your domain

findings.title: SQL injection (database error revealed)
findings.evidence: Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MySQL server version near '' at line
findings.fix: use parameterized prepared statements for every value, allowlist identifiers, least-privilege DB account
findings.impact: the query is attacker-influenced; data theft or modification may follow

findings.title: OS command injection
findings.evidence: server echoed injected marker QX608665b8af without the command text (separator '; echo')
findings.fix: never pass input to a shell; call fixed executables with argument arrays, allowlist inputs
findings.impact: the attacker runs arbitrary commands on your server, total compromise

findings.title: Admin surface reachable without login
findings.fix: deny by default: authenticate every route, then authorize by role, server-side
findings.impact: anyone can reach privileged pages and APIs

findings.title: Admin surface reachable without login
findings.fix: deny by default: authenticate every route, then authorize by role, server-side
findings.impact: anyone can reach privileged pages and APIs

findings.title: State-changing form without CSRF token
findings.evidence: POST form with fields: account, amount and no hidden CSRF token
findings.fix: add a per-session CSRF token (constant-time compare) and SameSite cookies; never rely on secrecy of URLs
findings.impact: a third-party page can submit this form with the victim logged in
findings.detail: confirm by replaying from a cross-origin page on a dry-run endpoint

findings.title: State-changing form without CSRF token
findings.evidence: POST form with fields: username, password and no hidden CSRF token
findings.fix: add a per-session CSRF token (constant-time compare) and SameSite cookies; never rely on secrecy of URLs
findings.impact: a third-party page can submit this form with the victim logged in
findings.detail: confirm by replaying from a cross-origin page on a dry-run endpoint

findings.title: No rate limit observed on login
findings.fix: layer limits (edge + app): e.g. 4/min then 10/10min then 20/hour per IP+account, count failures, add CAPTCHA
findings.impact: credential stuffing and password spraying run at scale
findings.detail: no 429/lockout observed in a gentle N=10 burst; manual review recommended before concluding

findings.title: Third-party script without Subresource Integrity
findings.fix: add integrity="sha384-..." and crossorigin to every cross-origin script/link, or self-host the asset
findings.impact: a compromised CDN silently runs attacker code in your pages

findings.title: Source map published
findings.fix: strip sourceMappingURL from shipped JS or serve .map files only for internal builds
findings.impact: original source (including comments and internal APIs) is recoverable

findings.title: Write methods accepted (PUT/DELETE)
findings.evidence: Allow: GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
findings.fix: reject non-GET/POST at the edge, require auth and CSRF on any allowed write method
findings.impact: unauthenticated file upload or deletion may be possible

findings.title: HTTP TRACE enabled
findings.evidence:
TRACE / HTTP/1.1
User-Agent: QuantIQRedTeamBot/1.0 (authorized self-testing)
Cookie:
findings.fix: disable TRACE at the server/proxy: nginx does not enable it by default, apache: TraceEnable off
findings.impact: cross-site tracing can echo custom headers back to scripts
